perf.summary: Type dispatch uses if/else-if on a small dense int set; an unhandled type silently no-ops.
perf.currentCost: Two sequential branch comparisons (==0 then ==1) per query iteration; documents nothing about type 2+.
perf.proposedChange: Keep the branch structure (it is already minimal), but reorder so the more frequent query path is tested first if profiling shows query-heavy workloads, or leave as-is. No code change strictly needed; the main observation is the silent no-op for type>1 is by design under 'unchecked Run'.
perf.rationale: Branch order can matter for predictor warmup, but with only two arms and data-dependent types the win is negligible. This is essentially already optimal.
perf.risk: None; reordering arms is semantics-preserving only if exactly one arm matches per type, which holds.
